This is an appeal filed under Section 14A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (SC/ST Act), challenging the order dated 14-08-2025 in Crl.M.C Jayesh N.K vs State Of Kerala on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186721387/

sentences.text:
The appellant is the accused in Crime No. 73/2025 of Vanitha Police Station, Kasaragod district,
which has been registered alleging commission of offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 376(2)(k) and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC), Section 64(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act.
3.

The allegation against the appellant/accused is that during the period between June 2015 and March 2020, and also on 21-05-2024, on the promise of marriage and under the threat that the nude pictures of the victim would be shared with the husband of the victim, the appellant 2025:KER:73680 CRL.A NO. 1800 OF 2025 committed rape on the victim.
It is alleged that the victim belongs to a Scheduled Caste community, and therefore, the appellant/accused had committed the offences alleged against him.

4. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant/accused submits that even according to the admitted case of the victim, the relationship between the victim and the appellant/accused lasted for a considerably long period between June 2015 and March 2020.

It is submitted that the victim got married in the month of January, 2024, and had, at any rate, a crime could not have been registered against the appellant/accused in the year 2025 on the allegation that the appellant/accused had committed rape on the victim on the false promise of marriage.
It is submitted that it is settled law that a breakdown of a longstanding relationship cannot thereafter be termed as rape on the false promise of marriage.
The learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposes the grant of bail.

It is pointed out that according to the victim, while the initial relationship between the victim and the appellant/accused was on the false promise of marriage, the appellant/accused thereafter withdrew from the promise of marriage and got married to another lady.

It is submitted that even after the marriage of the victim to another person, the appellant/accused had threatened to circulate the nude pictures of the victim to the husband of the victim and had forced her into sexual relationship in the month of May,
2024, and therefore, the appellant/accused has clearly committed the offences alleged against him.
It is pointed out that the appellant/accused is also accused of having committed the offence under Section 506 of the IPC (criminal intimidation).
It is submitted that the accused was arrested only on 22-07-2025.
It is confirmed that the investigation has been completed and the final report has been filed.
It is also confirmed that notice of this bail 2025:KER:73680 CRL.A NO. 1800 OF 2025 application has been served on the victim in Crime No.73/2025 of Vanitha Police Station, Kasaragod district.
6. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant/accused and the learned Public Prosecutor, I am of the view that the appellant/accused can be granted bail subject to conditions.
The investigation has been completed, and final report has already been filed.
The appellant/accused has been in custody for nearly 75 days.

Prima facie, there is merit in the Jayesh N.K vs State Of Kerala on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186721387/
2 contention taken by the learned counsel for the appellant/accused that the breakdown of a longstanding relationship cannot thereafter be depicted as rape.

entities.text: Jayesh N.K vs State Of Kerala on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The further detention of the appellant/accused does not appear necessary, at this stage.
7.
Accordingly, this appeal is allowed, and the impugned order dated 14-08-2025 in Crl.M.C No.1262/2025 on the file of the Court of Sessions, Kasaragod Division, will stand set aside.

If any of the aforesaid conditions are violated, the Investigating officer in Crime No.
73/2025 of Vanitha Police Station, Kasaragod district, may apply to the jurisdictional Court for cancellation of bail.

Sd/-
GOPINATH P. JUDGE ats Jayesh N.K vs State Of Kerala on 7 October, 2025
